## Teaching points

1. SGLT2 inhibitors can cause diabetic ketoacidosis with a normal or only mildly raised glucose; check the anion gap and blood ketones in any unwell patient taking one.
2. Typical precipitants are reduced intake (fasting, ketogenic diets), acute illness, surgery, insulin dose reduction and alcohol; several often combine.
3. Measure blood beta-hydroxybutyrate: the urine nitroprusside dipstick detects acetoacetate only and can underestimate ketosis.
4. Treat as DKA (fluids, insulin infusion, potassium) but give dextrose with the insulin from the start; stop the SGLT2 inhibitor.
5. Do not anchor on an obvious diagnosis: an unexplained high anion gap acidosis needs its own explanation.
